toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.methodChoice: Specification of where the departures fall (is/is-not comparison), then competing-hypotheses comparison, with a source check on the exit forms.
output.brief:
Resignations are concentrated in one place. Eight of the 11 associates on the Kestrel matter have left, against 1 of the 13 who never worked on it. Other groups are at normal levels, and the firm-wide hours increase applied everywhere, so it doesn't explain one group. Pay and general market movement look unlikely to be the main cause, because they would not hit one matter so unevenly. Pay can't be ruled out, though. Seven exit forms say "career opportunity". But leavers were told the group head might read those forms, so they are weak evidence.

Everything on Kestrel was supervised by one partner, Dorian Faulk. That means the records can't tell you whether the cause is the heavy workload or his supervision style. The survey comments point to both. Kestrel places also went to the associates with the most spare capacity, which doesn't change this.

Don't pay the group-wide retention payment and close the review. It would cost about £228k, aim at the wrong cause, and end the inquiry. Run the confidential outside interviews (about £9k, three weeks), designed to separate workload from supervision. Add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition tracking. Decide on contract reviewers or a change of supervisor after the interviews. Confidence is moderate: high that the problem is Kestrel-specific, low on which factor drives it.
